label: EU(7)-PIM: phenylpropanolamine, pseudoephedrine
title: Decongestant (pseudoephedrine or phenylpropanolamine) in an older person
statement: Norephedrine (=Phenylpropanolamine) | In lists: 3 (A) | Main reason: Higher risk of elevation of blood pressure secondary to sympathomimetic activity | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: (none stated) || Pseudoephedrine | In lists: 5 (B) | Main reason: Higher risk of elevation of blood pressure secondary to sympathomimetic activity | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Adjust dose in cases of renal failure; 15-30 mg three times per day for the treatment of urinary incontinence in older adults. M | Alternatives: (none stated)

plain_summary: Phenylpropanolamine and pseudoephedrine can raise blood pressure. The European list flags both for review in older people. Australian pseudoephedrine product information lists severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure, severe acute or chronic kidney disease, and kidney failure as reasons to avoid it.

medicine_groups.name: Pseudoephedrine and phenylpropanolamine (decongestants)
medicine_groups.note: Tablets and liquids count, including exact combination products that contain pseudoephedrine. Nurofen Cold & Flu with Decongestant contains ibuprofen and pseudoephedrine. Bare Nurofen Cold & Flu or a PE label does not identify pseudoephedrine. Codral Original Cold & Flu and Sudafed Sinus + Pain Relief contain paracetamol, so check other paracetamol supplies separately. Phenylpropanolamine is also called norephedrine; neither has a current Australian brand listed. Phenylephrine is not in this group. Bare Demazin, bare Sudafed and Codral Cold & Flu without Original are not accepted as identifying pseudoephedrine.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a person aged 65 or over is supplied any Group A medicine (pseudoephedrine, phenylpropanolamine or norephedrine), alone or in a combination product. For a brand-only row, the exact product name must be listed in Group A; bare Demazin, bare Sudafed or Codral Cold & Flu without Original is not enough to identify pseudoephedrine. If a qualifying Group A supply is present and age is missing, report only a possible finding and ask whether the person is 65 or older.
cannot_be_seen: When no relevant result or observation lines are recorded: blood pressure readings and kidney function. The record also does not show the reason for purchase (cold, sinus or bladder control) or other cold products bought elsewhere.
ask_the_gp: A check of the person's blood pressure and whether a decongestant is suitable for them, with kidney function in mind when pseudoephedrine is used.
